subject: Observability credit phasing & rollover options for Q3 expansion
messages:
From: Linh Tran <linh@brightline.health>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightline.health>
Date: 2028-03-05T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Observability add-on pricing questions for Q3 expansion

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the dashboards and trace playback look like a good fit for our clinical analytics team. We're sizing the Q3 expansion and have two quick asks around the observability add-ons: retention (long-term spans), tracing ingest, and the advanced dashboards pack.

1) Do you offer phased crediting if we commit to a 12-month expansion (start small months 1-3, ramp months 4-12)?
2) Can unused credits roll over quarter-to-quarter or do they expire at month end?
3) Any special considerations in pricing if we move to a seatless dashboard model (ingest-metered only)?

Attached is our Q2 telemetry summary to help size. Procurement asked that we get a clear proposal we can show our CFO. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if needed.

Cheers,
Linh
Director, Data Platform
Brightline Health
attachments: brightline_q2_telemetry_summary.csv (csv, 124KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh@brightline.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-05T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-on pricing questions for Q3 expansion

Hi Linh — thanks for the file, that helps a lot. Looping in Ben (pricing lead) and Marissa (CS) so we can give concrete options. Quick answers up front:

- We support phased credit schedules tied to committed ARR; months 1-3 can be lower committed volumes with a gated ramp to the full commit in month 4.
- By default credits are quarterly and do not roll forward; we can offer a limited rollover policy for multi-quarter commitments (details below).
- Seatless dashboard (ingest-only) is supported; pricing is slightly higher on per-ingest unit to account for visualization compute, but we can offer a blended rate depending on estimated token/ingest mix.

Ben — can you propose two pricing constructs (1: slabless paygo with 10% volume discount at >X ingest; 2: 12-month commit with phased credits and 8% committed discount + limited rollover)? Marissa — can you confirm operational impacts for retention increases (SLA, storage class changes)?

Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh@brightline.health>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-06T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-on pricing questions for Q3 expansion

Hi Linh — appreciate the detail and the telemetry export. I ran rough numbers against your ingest profile; preliminary constructs below (all $ numbers are illustrative until legal/finance approves a formal SOW):

Option A — Flexible (slabless)- Ingest-metered pricing: $0.025 per ingestion unit; advanced dashboards: $1,200 / month (seatless bundle).
- Volume tiers: 5% discount > 1M units/mo, 10% discount > 3M units/mo.
- Credits: monthly consumption, no rollover.

Option B — 12-month Commit (phased ramp)- Yearly commit priced at $X/month equivalent (we'll put numbers in the SOW).- Phasing: months 1-3 at 40% of full committed credits, months 4-12 at 100% of committed credits.
- Rollover: up to 10% unused credits can carry to next quarter; at year-end remainder expires.
- SLA uplift: included for commits > $150k/year (lower latency tracing retention, 99.9% ingest availability).

Operational note: increasing long-term span retention beyond default 30 days will move archival to colder storage after 90 days; this changes restore times (we can document TTR).

Attachments: proposed-sow-observability.pdf (draft with sample numbers)

If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute pricing review tomorrow; otherwise I'll convert Option B into a priced SOW.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-sow-observability.pdf (pdf, 86KB)
From: Linh Tran <linh@brightline.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightline.health>
Date: 2028-03-07T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-on pricing questions for Q3 expansion

Thanks Ben — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of follow-ups from CFO/Procurement after reviewing Option B:

1) Rollover policy: can we increase carryover to 20% for the first year only (we'll be less predictable during onboarding)?
2) SLA uplift: can the 99.9% ingest availability be written into a clause with credits for missed targets (standard SLO credit formula)?
3) Phasing: can the months 1-3 be split 30% / 60% / 80% instead of flat 40%? That maps better to our hiring ramp.

If you can update the SOW with those three asks, Procurement is ready to review on their side and push to legal. Happy to take a 20-minute call to align on (2).

Linh
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh@brightline.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-09T16:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-on pricing questions for Q3 expansion

Hi Linh — quick update after internal alignment:

- We can accommodate a 20% first-year carryover for unused credits; we will add a clause that carryover decays to 10% in year two (if applicable).
- Ben will include a standard SLO credit schedule for the 99.9% ingest availability; legal typically prefers the SLO mapped to revenue credits (we'll draft the specific formula).
- Phasing: we can change the ramp profile to 30% / 60% / 80% for months 1-3.

Ben — please update the attached SOW with these concessions and a priced example using Brightline's Q2 profile. Marissa — once we have the SOW Ben will work with you to nominate operational playbooks for retention changes.

Next steps: Ben to deliver revised SOW by EOD Friday; Linh/Procurement to confirm internal sign-off and we schedule legal review.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
